messages:
incidents-bot: Paging: p99 streaming tail latency > 2.0s observed in eu-west-2 for streaming-proxy-prod (~15% of requests) — auto-page to oncall

jared (oncall): seeing the page. I have the live pager, standing by. Any customer-facing alerts yet? :eyes:

sasha (sre): confirmed p95 up ~700ms, p99 spike to ~2.4s. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/streaming/streaming-tail?orgId=1&from=now-30m to 1765439999. Streaming stalls coincide with increased NAT retransmits in flow logs.

priya (neteng): looking at VPC egress path for eu-west-2. I can already see periodic packet drops and TLS handshake retries concentrated between subnets azb->azc. NAT gateway SNAT table shows ephemeral port reuse spikes.

jared (oncall): customer-impact: minimal error rate increase, but latency visible for a handful of long-lived sessions (streaming tail). Emily, anything from support?

emily (cust-succ): one active customer on a demo stream reported delayed tokens, they called at 09:12UTC. No escalations yet. I told them we're investigating and offered a workaround (switch to non-streaming fallback).

dom (runtime): logs from proxy show many stalled chunk writes with "write: connection reset by peer" and long backpressure in the request pipeline. KV cache hits unaffected. Suspect network-level retransmits rather than runtime CPU.

luis (infra): running a quick check: NAT SNAT utilization at 82% on nat-01, ephemeral ports dipping low around the spike windows. No node restarts. Routing tables stable.

priya (neteng): can we confirm cross-az hairpin? I see some traffic egressing nat-01 in azb then re-entering azc path due to recent route-policy change last week (route-policy 2026-03-01).

jared (oncall): action list: 1) Priya to validate and if necessary pin traffic to local NAT with steering. 2) Luis to provision temporary extra nat-01-ephemeral pool or enable port-forwarding mitigation. 3) Sasha + Dom to monitor streaming tail metrics and enable graceful fallback (non-streaming) for affected sessions. 4) Emily to update affected customer. 

sasha (sre): starting live mitigations: enabling aggressive TCP keepalive to detect stalls faster and reduce handshake retries. Also rolling back the route-policy change in azb that may cause hairpin (will do a canary first, 1 host).

priya (neteng): canary rollback applied to 1 host in azb (host-azb-02). Observing immediate drop in retransmits for flows routed locally. Will escalate to roll back across azb if stable for 3 minutes.

luis (infra): provisioning a temporary NAT-ephemeral extender (nat-01-ext) now — ETA ~4m. I'll also increase SNAT port range on nat-02 one-off to spread load.

jared (oncall): @emily please tell the demo customer we're applying network mitigations; ask to retry in 10 mins. No need to acknowledge to all customers yet.

emily (cust-succ): message sent. They appreciated the update and will test again in ~10.

dom (runtime): enabling fallback flag on streaming-proxy for sessions exceeding 1.5s tail for 30s window. This will pull affected sessions to non-streaming path automatically. Deploying now (patch id: rwd-deploy/stream-fallback-2026-17654).

sasha (sre): metrics after canary (2m): p99 down from 2.4s -> 1.1s on canary path. Retransmit rate falling. Good signal. Recommend rolling route-policy rollback across azb.

priya (neteng): rolling rollback to azb complete. Cross-az hairpin metric normalized. Continuing to monitor.

luis (infra): nat-01-ext is up and bound. SNAT pool spread reduced ephemeral usage to 45%. No errors on provisioning.

jared (oncall): current state: mitigations in place (route rollback + nat extender + runtime fallback). p95 ~ 600ms, p99 ~ 850ms. Streaming stalls reduced to baseline. I'm going to page the oncall rotation for a 30min handoff watch in case of rebound.

emily (cust-succ): reported customer retried and confirmed stream is smooth now. No follow-ups.

sasha (sre): adding checklist for post-incident: 1) confirm route-policy change owner and rationale (who approved 2026-03-01) 2) schedule permanent NAT capacity increase or autoscale 3) add alert: NAT ephemeral saturation > 70% + cross-az retransmit correlation -> auto-evict route-policy change rollbacks.

priya (neteng): note: route-policy change came from infra config roll last week (ansible commit 7f3a). I'll open PR to remove hairpin rule and add guardrails.

jared (oncall): tagging as "monitoring" for now. If metrics stay stable 30m, we'll close. Great work all. :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: Incident update: mitigations applied by jared, priya, luis, sasha, dom at 1765439999 - 1765441200. Incident status: mitigated (monitoring). Runbook reference: nat-ephemeral-handoff -> https://runbooks.redwood.internal/nat-ephemeral-handoff
